item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly To Dump Heavy Rain On The Caribbean
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Tropical Storm Dolly is expected to bring heavy rain to the Caribbean Islands this weekend. The storm currently has sustained winds of 40 miles per hour as it races across the Atlantic, and is expected to weaken as it reaches the islands. Forecasters warn, however, that it could still produce heavy rain in parts of the Caribbean. The Leeward…
item.content:encoded: Tropical Storm Dolly is expected to bring heavy rain to the Caribbean Islands this weekend. The storm currently has sustained winds of 40 miles per hour as it races across the Atlantic, and is expected to weaken as it reaches the islands. Forecasters warn, however, that it could still produce heavy rain in parts of the Caribbean. The Leeward Islands could see heavy rain on Saturday, with Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands getting hit on Sunday and Monday. Island residents are being told to prepare for gusty winds and flash flooding.

item.title: DeSantis Slams Grand Jury Report
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis is pushing back hard against a grand jury report that says ten-million dollars from a Medicaid settlement was improperly steered through the Hope Florida Foundation for political purposes. Speaking Thursday in Lake City, DeSantis called the report's findings false, insisting the money was a legal, private contribution — not…
item.content:encoded: Governor Ron DeSantis is pushing back hard against a grand jury report that says ten-million dollars from a Medicaid settlement was improperly steered through the Hope Florida Foundation for political purposes. Speaking Thursday in Lake City, DeSantis called the report's findings false, insisting the money was a legal, private contribution — not diverted Medicaid funds. He labeled the entire investigation a politically motivated "hoax" targeting his administration and First Lady Casey DeSantis.The governor stressed the grand jury found no probable cause for criminal charges. The report claims the money helped fund opposition to a marijuana legalization amendment.

item.title: UWF Stuns No. 16 Southern Illinois in Historic Division I Football Debut
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The University of West Florida marked a milestone Thursday night with a stunning 34-31 victory over nationally-ranked Southern Illinois in its first-ever Division I football game. Playing at home, the Argonauts defeated the No. 16-ranked Salukis in a matchup that signaled UWF's successful transition to the higher level of college athletics. The…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida marked a milestone Thursday night with a stunning 34-31 victory over nationally-ranked Southern Illinois in its first-ever Division I football game. Playing at home, the Argonauts defeated the No. 16-ranked Salukis in a matchup that signaled UWF's successful transition to the higher level of college athletics.

The win represents a landmark moment for the university's football program, which only recently moved up from Division II. UWF's defense held strong down the stretch to secure the upset victory, suggesting the program may have the talent and coaching to compete effectively at the Division I level from the start.

The Argonauts will look to build on the momentum from their historic home opener when they travel to Central Arkansas next Saturday, September 5, for their second Division I contest. Early success could help establish UWF as a competitive newcomer to the FCS ranks.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment-based contractor faces significant prison time after a jury swiftly found him guilty of racketeering and organized fraud charges Thursday. Jesse Wayne LaCoste was convicted on the charges involving sums exceeding $50,000, according to court records from the North Escambia area.

The six-person jury deliberated for less than an hour before reaching its verdict, suggesting little disagreement among jurors on the evidence presented during trial. The quick turnaround indicates prosecutors built a strong case against LaCoste regarding his business practices and alleged fraudulent operations.

Details regarding sentencing have not yet been announced. LaCoste's conviction marks the resolution of what investigators described as a scheme that impacted multiple victims in the Escambia County area.

item.content:encoded: The Alabama Attorney General's office has upheld murder and burglary convictions against Frank Cortez McQueen, 46, of Evergreen, according to WKRG News 5. The decision affirms convictions on both charges for McQueen in connection with a case in Conecuh County. While the case involves an Alabama defendant, the ruling represents a significant development in a high-profile criminal matter in the region. McQueen had challenged the convictions on appeal, but the attorney general's office determined the original verdicts should stand. The case involved charges related to both a homicide and a property crime, which are among the most serious felonies prosecuted in the state.

item.title: UWF Argos win historic first D-I football game, top Southern Illinois 37-34
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The University of West Florida's football program reached a major milestone Saturday, notching its first victory as a Division I team with a 37-34 home win over Southern Illinois at Pen-Air Field. The Argos' debut in the FCS ranks came against the Salukis in front of their home crowd, and UWF made the most of the opportunity. The victory marks an…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's football program reached a major milestone Saturday, notching its first victory as a Division I team with a 37-34 home win over Southern Illinois at Pen-Air Field.

The Argos' debut in the FCS ranks came against the Salukis in front of their home crowd, and UWF made the most of the opportunity. The victory marks an important early validation for the program's move up from Division II, a transition that reshaped Pensacola's college sports landscape.

According to WKRG News 5, the game was decided in close fashion, suggesting UWF's defense and offense both stepped up when it mattered most in their inaugural D-I contest. The win gives the Argos early momentum as they settle into their new competitive level and continue their schedule this season.

item.content:encoded:
The UMS-Wright Bulldogs cheer squad has been selected as WKRG News 5's Cheer Squad of the Week to kick off the 2026 high school football season, according to the station's announcement.

Coach Shay Owen leads the program, which fields both a varsity squad of 13 members and a JV squad of 21 cheerleaders. The recognition marks the start of what WKRG says will be a weekly feature highlighting area cheer programs throughout the season.

The selection comes as high schools across the region gear up for fall football, with cheerleaders set to take their place in the stands and on the sidelines.

item.content:encoded:
A state representative in Mobile is giving residents a chance to weigh in on what to call the new I-10 bridge spanning the Mobile River. According to WKRG News 5, State Representative Barbara Drummond is launching a community naming effort for the infrastructure project, inviting Mobile County residents to submit suggestions.

The initiative reflects a broader trend of public engagement in major infrastructure projects, allowing communities to have a voice in how their regional landmarks are identified. While the bridge itself is a significant undertaking for the Mobile area, the naming process offers residents an opportunity to participate in shaping local identity.

Details on how residents can submit naming suggestions and the timeline for the selection process have not yet been announced. For more information, residents should check with their state representative's office or local Mobile County government channels.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue responded to a residential structure fire Tuesday, successfully evacuating two residents and three dogs from the burning home without any injuries, according to WKRG News 5.

Fire crews arrived at the scene and worked quickly to locate and remove the occupants and their pets before the fire could spread further. No injuries were reported among the residents, firefighters, or animals involved in the incident.

The details surrounding the cause of the fire and extent of damage to the structure have not yet been released by fire officials.

City officials in Prichard, Alabama gathered this week to hash out a $21.8 million budget that comes at a critical juncture for the municipality. Mayor and all five council members convened to discuss how the spending plan will impact various city services, particularly the police department.

The budget discussions arrive during what city leadership described as a period of transition and uncertainty for the community. While specifics on how the plan affects police operations weren't detailed, the department's funding appears to be a central concern as officials weigh competing priorities for the coming fiscal year.

According to reporting from WKRG News 5, the full scope of budget allocations and any changes to municipal services should become clearer as the council moves forward with formal approval steps.

item.title: Semmes officers mow elderly resident's overgrown yard, earn community award
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: A couple of Semmes police officers went above and beyond their usual patrol duties this week, earning recognition for helping an elderly woman tackle an overwhelming yard maintenance problem. Sergeant Brian Fillingim and Corporal Hand noticed the woman's grass and weeds had grown considerably during a call to her home. Rather than leave it at…
item.content:encoded: A couple of Semmes police officers went above and beyond their usual patrol duties this week, earning recognition for helping an elderly woman tackle an overwhelming yard maintenance problem. Sergeant Brian Fillingim and Corporal Hand noticed the woman's grass and weeds had grown considerably during a call to her home. Rather than leave it at that, the officers decided to take action themselves. "We responded to a call at her house and we realized the grass was getting really tall, so myself and Corporal Hand spoke about it when it was over," Fillingim explained. The officers' initiative didn't go unnoticed. Their work earned them the Smiles Behind the Shield Award, recognition that highlights the kind of community-focused policing that builds trust between law enforcement and the neighborhoods they serve. The gesture underscores how small acts of service—especially for vulnerable residents who may struggle with physical tasks—can make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

item.content:encoded:
The Gulf Coast has plenty to offer this weekend if you're looking to get out of the house. Among the highlights: an immersive dinosaur experience is coming to the Mobile Convention Center, featuring life-sized prehistoric creatures that promise to transport visitors back millions of years.

According to WKRG News 5, the weekend also features a tribute to the King of Pop and events geared toward card collectors, giving families and entertainment fans multiple options across the region.

The full slate of five recommended events runs through Sunday, Aug. 30, with activities spread across the Gulf Coast area.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Mobile cut the ribbon Thursday on a new senior center serving the Hillsdale community, according to WKRG News 5. The facility, named after the late John E. King—a longtime deacon and community leader in Mobile—will provide a gathering space for senior citizens in the area.

City officials and members of the community attended the opening ceremony to celebrate the new resource. The center represents an expansion of senior services in Mobile County, offering seniors in the Hillsdale area a dedicated space for activities and programming.

King's legacy as a faith leader and advocate for his community made him a fitting namesake for the center, which now bears his name.

item.content:encoded: Most Escambia County government offices will shut down on Monday, Sept. 7, for the Labor Day holiday, according to WKRG News 5. Residents and businesses needing county services should plan accordingly, as the closures will affect numerous departments throughout the county. All closed offices are scheduled to reopen Tuesday, Sept. 8, resuming normal business hours. County officials encourage anyone with urgent matters to contact offices before the holiday weekend or wait until the following week to conduct business.

item.title: Gulf Islands National Seashore updates personal watercraft wake zones
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The National Park Service has announced adjustments to wake zones for personal watercraft operating along the Gulf Islands National Seashore, which stretches across the Panhandle including waters off Pensacola and Santa Rosa County. According to WKRG News 5, the changes to the regulated wake zones are intended to better manage recreational boating…
item.content:encoded:
The National Park Service has announced adjustments to wake zones for personal watercraft operating along the Gulf Islands National Seashore, which stretches across the Panhandle including waters off Pensacola and Santa Rosa County.

According to WKRG News 5, the changes to the regulated wake zones are intended to better manage recreational boating activity in the protected marine areas. The seashore encompasses roughly 150 miles of pristine coastline and waters that see significant seasonal boat traffic from both local residents and visitors.

The National Park Service manages these zones to balance recreation with environmental protection, including safeguarding seagrass beds and marine habitats that are critical to the Gulf's ecosystem. Personal watercraft operators in the area should review the updated regulations before heading out on the water.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Gets $25K Grant for Cat Trap-Neuter-Return Program
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The Santa Rosa County Animal Shelter has secured a $25,000 grant from Florida Animal Friend to expand its Trap-Neuter-Return program, according to county officials. The funding will help the shelter continue its efforts to manage the feral cat population in the county through humane methods. The Trap-Neuter-Return program catches stray and feral…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Animal Shelter has secured a $25,000 grant from Florida Animal Friend to expand its Trap-Neuter-Return program, according to county officials.

The funding will help the shelter continue its efforts to manage the feral cat population in the county through humane methods. The Trap-Neuter-Return program catches stray and feral cats, has them spayed or neutered, and returns them to their original locations, reducing reproduction and preventing the need for euthanasia.

This grant represents a significant boost to the shelter's animal welfare initiatives in Santa Rosa County.
